explanation: The vulnerable HMACAlgorithm.sign feeds whatever key material OctKey yields directly into hmac.new with no empty-key rejection; OctKey.import_key only warns (SecurityWarning) for keys under 14 bytes and lets a zero-length key through. An empty HMAC key is a degenerate case of inadequate cryptographic strength (CWE-326): the MAC is computable by anyone with no secret knowledge, enabling forged HS256/HS384/HS512 JWTs when the application's secret resolves to '' or None (a common misconfiguration). The fixed code adds a hard rejection of empty op_key in sign (and, per the advisory, verify and OctKey.import_key), materially correcting the defect. The fix commit, vulnerable code, PoC, and affected-version range (<= 1.6.7, fixed in 1.6.8) are all supplied and consistent.
finding: HMAC sign/verify accepts empty key material: OctKey with zero-length raw_value is passed to hmac.new, producing an attacker-reproducible digest; reject empty keys before use.
note: Supplied code pair shows only the sign() function; the verify() counterpart and the OctKey.import_key reject are described in the advisory text but not included in the pair. CWE-326 is the closest taxonomy fit; the condition is operator-misconfiguration-dependent (empty secret), which tempers severity from CRITICAL.
